absent: Encoding and flag values of DAX entries and order extraction are not shown.
Entry lock, wait, wake and busy page decision internals are not shown.
Device direct access, flush and read lock semantics are not shown.
PMD geometry constants and check scheduling interval values are not shown.
Page cache tag numbers and xarray error and mark mechanics are not shown.
Fault, folio, rmap and writeback infrastructure beyond touched members is not shown.
Caller locking for truncate and punch paths beyond the stated requirement is not shown.

findings.text: Lock lookup for one file offset returns either a locked stored entry plus its struct page, or a distinguished all-ones cookie when absent or zero or empty with no page output. Unlock accepts the cookie and ignores it, otherwise releases the indicated locked entry.

Busy scan over a byte interval unmaps the interval first, then walks stored entries and returns the first page still pinned, or null when none is busy or the mapping is not DAX. Whole mapping variant scans from start to maximal end.
Single index removal invalidates in truncate mode and warns when nothing was removed. Range removal walks an index interval and detaches every stored value entry.

Layout break repeatedly scans for a busy page in a byte range, waits for it to become idle with a caller supplied callback, then deletes the range once quiet. Final variant scans the whole mapping and waits uninterruptibly until quiet before deleting.
Synchronous single index invalidation only removes clean entries. Mapping writeback flushes dirty shared entries over a writeback control range and records errors on the mapping.
File unshare copies shared extents over a clamped file range using write plus unshare plus DAX iteration, doing nothing when the start is outside current size.

Small helpers expose read locking around the interval mapping lock, effective iterator length trimmed by destination and source extents, full advance of the iterator, preferred source selection, and a predicate for shared destination needing copy from a mapped source.

DAX state lives as encoded values in the address space page tree with a page count adjusted by entry order. Insertions add one shifted by order, removals subtract one shifted by the removed entry order, and PMD join removal subtracts the PMD page count.
Absent, zero and empty positions are not errors for lock lookup. They yield the sentinel cookie and leave the page output untouched, while present entries yield a locked entry and its page.

Entry acquisition prefers an existing unlocked entry, signals fallback on conflict, signals IO failure on non value storage, downgrades PMD zero or empty entries to PTE scope with unmap and detach when order zero is wanted, otherwise locks the found entry or installs a new locked empty entry with PMD marking for larger order, retrying on allocation pressure.
Single entry invalidation without truncate keeps entries marked dirty or towrite. With truncate it always detaches. It reports whether an entry was detached and adjusts accounting by entry order.
Dirty range clearing walks the interval, skips absent entries, and clears both dirty and towrite marks on each present locked entry before releasing it for the next waiter.
Writeback requires page sized blocks, a non empty mapping and full sync mode. It tags the interval for writeback, then processes each tagged entry individually, stopping on first failure.

Per entry writeback reconciles a locked entry by relookup, bails when punched or reallocated to another frame or already untagged, otherwise locks it, clears towrite early under the tree lock, aligns PMD indexes down, write protects all mapped intervals, flushes caches, then clears dirty and wakes the next waiter.

Direct access resolves a file position to a device page offset, checks that the device returned enough contiguous frames with required alignment when a frame number is wanted, and fails when no kernel address is returned while one was requested.

Copy around an unaligned interval inside an aligned destination either zeroes or copies only head and tail edges, zeroes the whole aligned span for holes or shared or unwritten sources, flushes after zeroing, and reports IO failure on copy faults.

Hole faults install zero entries and map the small or huge zero page. PMD hole handling has two builds, one attempting huge zero page insertion and falling back when unavailable, the other always falling back.

Unshare iteration advances unchanged when no copy is wanted. Otherwise it expands the byte range to page boundaries, invalidates cached pages over that expanded range, takes both destination and source direct addresses, and copies the full expanded length.
A fault counts as synchronous only when the iterator is for write, the area requests synchronous mapping, and the extent is marked dirty.

Insertion of a new frame marks the host dirty for asynchronous writes, unmaps replaced zero or shared ranges, associates the new entry while detaching the old zero or empty or shared entry, keeps an existing normal entry instead of replacing it, and sets dirty and shared write marks as appropriate.
Copy on write from DAX resolves the source extent position, maps the faulting anonymous page atomically, copies one page from the device address, then unmaps.

The page tree interrupt safe lock guards loads, stores and mark checks. Holders drop it before sleeping for an entry, before unmapping pages, before cache flush and rmap walk, and before voluntary reschedule, then reacquire and resume the walk.

Per entry locking serializes faults against truncate, punch, writeback and scanning. Waiters block until unlocked, exclusive scans take ownership before acting, and releasers wake either all waiters after removal or only the next waiter after transient handling.

Lock lookup holds RCU across the tree walk but releases it while waiting. Direct access and unshare copies hold the DAX read lock. Writeback holds the file interval map read lock while write protecting every area mapping an index interval.
Relevant address space state comprises the page tree, the resident page count, the backing host inode, and the interval mapping semaphore used for read side rmap walks.

Relevant iterator and control state comprises file position and length, owning inode, operation flags and status, destination and optional source extents with offset length address device type and flags, plus writeback range bounds and sync mode.

An index moves from absent to locked empty, to associated present with optional zero or PMD character, to dirty or towrite when written shared, back to clean after flush, and to detached plus tree cleared on truncate punch or layout break.
Layout break loops between scan and idle wait while a busy page exists, exits on wait interruption or missing callback, and only deletes the interval after observing no busy page.
Idle waiting has interruptible and uninterruptible forms keyed on a per page idle predicate, the former reporting interruption to the layout break caller.

Callers are truncate and hole punch for deletion, writeback for range flush, page faults for insert and hole load, and layout break around operations needing no active direct mappings such as unshare preparation.
Long walks pause the iterator, release the tree lock and reschedule periodically to avoid monopolizing CPU and blocking updates.

Unexpected states trigger one time warnings, including non value storage where an encoded entry is required, a missing entry during truncate style delete, page tagged dirty inside a DAX tree, and block size other than page size for writeback.
A maximal signed end offset selects scan or delete through the end of the file and is expanded to the maximal unsigned page index, while finite byte bounds are converted by page shift.
Allocation and conflict outcomes are reported with distinct fault codes for out of memory, bus error on IO failure, and fallback requesting a non DAX path.
